title: Sports Retailer

source.note: The book labels this "Sports Manufacturer"; the client is a retailer.

prompt: Your client is a sports retailer. They see strong opportunity in the post-COVID world and want growth recommendations. What would you do?

facts.reveal: Primarily offline physical stores, with limited online.
Footwear and apparel make up most of sales; equipment is small but growing.
They want to double revenue in 18–24 months. Organic first; inorganic if it accelerates results.
Any increase in price would lead to customers shifting to competition.
Order value is quite low: about ₹850 on average, around the price of a dry-fit T-shirt. There aren't many customers coming back.
Going back to acquiring new customers, how would you do that?
What about new markets? How would you scale there?
What other things can the client look at?

crux.statement: Price is locked, so doubling has to come first from basket size (₹850 is low) and frequency (few come back), then from new customers and places. The post-COVID fitness shift is why home fitness and athleisure are the right new categories.
crux.clue: "Order value is quite low… there aren't many customers coming back."

paths: Revenue per customer (price, basket, frequency) × number of customers (existing markets, new markets, new segments), then inorganic options

wrongTurns.text: Jumping straight to Tier 2 and 3 expansion

answerKey: Basket: bundles and kits, accessory zones at checkout
New customers: local events, gym partnerships, services, new categories, new segments (kids, women, corporates), compact stores in smaller cities
Inorganic, last: a fitness app, a home-fitness maker, academy or school joint ventures

close.condition: The candidate has identified basket and frequency as the gap and covered customer acquisition.
close.prompt: What are your final recommendations to the client?

anchors.s5: A long, unprioritised list of ideas.
anchors.s7: Structured levers, with basket and frequency identified as the gap.
anchors.s9: Prioritises by the facts given, sequences organic before inorganic, and checks whether the levers can plausibly reach 2X.

verifierFlags.text: No quant moment in the source; an illustration (customers × basket × visits must multiply to 2) was suggested.
verifierFlags.decision: No quant moment. The interviewer does not ask for one; a candidate who checks feasibility unprompted is credited at the top anchor.
